name: Piktochart
summary: Infographic, report and poster maker with template libraries and AI credits. The free plan limits downloads, Pro is priced per member, and PDF and PowerPoint export start on the Business tier.
best_for: individuals and small teams who need infographics, data-heavy reports and posters to look designed without hiring a designer — and above all students, teachers and nonprofits, for whom $39.99 and $60 a member a year with PDF and PowerPoint export are the best-value doors on the page
skip_if: you mainly need slides, because tools built for presentations do that better for the money. Skip it too if you need PDF or PowerPoint export but were budgeting for Pro, since those formats only start at Business. And skip it if you were counting on a real free tier, because two downloads is a demo rather than a plan — or if your AI use is heavy, since the credit allowances are capped and the page never prices a top-up
honest_knock:
The ladder here is not about how much you make, it is about which file you are allowed to hand over. Pro — the tier the page marks most popular — exports PNG only. PDF and PowerPoint are Business features, which the full feature table confirms in a single row most people scroll past. So if the reason you want this is to email a PDF handout or drop slides into a deck, Pro at $10 a member a month is not a cheaper Piktochart — it is the wrong product. Your real entry price is $17 a member a month on annual billing, or $20 monthly.

The free plan reads as generous and is not. Unlimited projects, two downloads — and not two a month: the comparison table lists the number of downloads as a flat 2. In our test on 20 October 2026 that counter ran per account, not per design: 2, then 1, then 0 across two different designs, and the third try opened 'You have run out of free downloads.' That is enough to find out whether you like the editor, which is a fair trial, but it is not the working free tier some competitors in this category offer, so do not plan around it.

The third thing to price is the AI credits: 60 on Free, 500 on Pro, 1,000 on Business. The pricing page does not say what one credit buys or what happens when you run out. The app says more, but not all of it: in our test on 20 October 2026 the AI infographic button said 1 credit, yet the free balance went from 60 to 57 after two failed attempts and one that worked, and the app sold one-off top-up packs from $20 for 2,000 credits. If AI generation is the reason you are buying, try it on Free first and watch the counter, because that meter can decide your bill.

One last piece of arithmetic. The annual discount is 33% on Pro but only 15% on Business, so the saving shrinks exactly at the tier most teams that need PDF or PowerPoint end up on. And if you have an educational email address or nonprofit status the picture changes completely: Education is $39.99 per member for a whole year and Nonprofit is $60, against $120 for a year of Pro, and both include the PDF and PowerPoint exports that Pro does not. Read the discount labels on those two with a squint, though. The FAQ calls them 76% and 64% off 'our annual pricing', which works back to about $167 a year — neither the $120 the same FAQ quotes for annual Pro nor the $180 that monthly Pro annualises to. The prices are real and cheap; the percentages are measured against a list price the page never shows you.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (re-verified 6 September and again 19 September 2026 on piktochart.com/pricing/, US dollar view; the plan amounts are unchanged from our 6 August 2026 reading) Free is $0, Pro is $15 per member per month billed monthly or $10 billed annually ($120 a year), Business is $20 monthly or $17 billed annually ($204 a year), and Enterprise is quote-only from 101 members. Free stops at 2 PNG downloads — a flat total, not two a month — 1 GB of storage, 60 AI credits and free templates only, and is capped at four members (one owner plus three). Pro adds unlimited PNG downloads, premium templates and icons, 500 AI credits and 100 GB, and the annual rate is what the page calls 33% off. Business, 15% off annually, adds PDF and PowerPoint export on top of PNG, the Brand Kit (unlimited brand colours, fonts and logos), 1,000 AI credits and 250 GB. Enterprise adds SSO/SAML, workspace management, a dedicated account manager and a one-off hour of training. Three further cards on the same page price other audiences, and two of them beat Pro on both price and capability. Education is $39.99 per member billed annually — the card splits the cents into a separate element, which is why a careless reading gives $39; the FAQ prints the full figure — with 250 AI credits, a limited Brand Kit and unlimited PNG, PDF and PowerPoint downloads, and requires a valid educational email address. Campus is quote-only above 3,000 seats. Nonprofit is $60 per member billed annually with the same 250 credits, limited Brand Kit and unlimited PNG, PDF and PPT downloads. The page's own FAQ calls those two 'a 76% discount' and 'a 64% discount' from its annual pricing, which works back to a list of about $167 a year — a figure that appears nowhere on the page, where annual Pro is $120 and monthly Pro annualises to $180. The page can be switched between USD, GBP, EUR, SGD, MXN and INR. No free trial is offered on the paid tiers — the free plan is the trial — and you can cancel anytime, though the FAQ adds that refunds are generally not given under the Terms of Use and are reviewed case by case, and that purchases of $168 or more can be settled by bank deposit.

compare_with.name: Canva
compare_with.why: the comparison nearly everybody actually makes, and it comes down to two questions rather than feature counts. First, check where each tool puts the file format you need, not what the headline costs. Piktochart keeps PDF and PowerPoint behind Business at $17 a member a month on annual billing, and a rival that includes your format one tier down is cheaper than its price list suggests. Second, be honest about what you are making — Piktochart is at its strongest on data-heavy infographics and reports and weaker as a general-purpose design tool, and if it is really slides you want then Beautiful.ai and Gamma are the closer peers. We have not read Canva's, Beautiful.ai's or Gamma's price lists ourselves, so verify theirs as well as ours; the Piktochart figures here were read on 2026-08-06.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 20 October 2026 on a new Free account (Daan created it and our AI assistant ran the test in his browser; nothing was paid and no card was entered): we made the same small infographic, titled TESTHAVEN with the figures 12, 8 and 20, once from a free template and once with the Pikto AI generator, changed its colour and font, and downloaded until the free downloads ran out.
findings: Free gives 2 PNG downloads per account, not per design: the download panel went from '2 Downloads Left' to 1 and then 0 across two different designs. A third try opened 'You have run out of free downloads.' with 'Choose your plan', and no file came.

PNG is the only free file format. PDF and PowerPoint carry a BUSINESS label, and choosing PDF opened an upgrade window straight away. Normal, Medium and High quality were all open on Free; a transparent background asked for an upgrade.

The AI generator was not reliable for us. The button said 1 credit, two of our three attempts ended in an error ('Probeer later opnieuw', try again later), and the balance went from 60 to 57 for one finished infographic. Whether each failed attempt cost a credit or the one that worked cost three is not clear from what we saw.

The AI kept all three numbers ('Appels: 12', 'Peren: 8', 'Bananen: 20': apples, pears, bananas) but extended our title to 'TESTHAVEN Fruit Inventaris' and added sentences of its own ('Perfect voor een gezonde snack of in een taart', 'Perfect for a healthy snack or in a cake'). The app warns that AI content may be inaccurate.
In the AI design's export the heading 'TOTAAL' in the closing block overlapped the paragraph below it, leaving part of it unreadable, and the photo next to 'Peren: 8' showed no pears.
Both downloads arrived as separate PNG files, not a ZIP: 800x1807 px (315 KB) for the template design and 800x2075 px (552 KB) for the AI design, each with our title and the three correct numbers.

The free template we used ('Food Safety Starts With You') was quick to edit: double-click, select all, type, and it saved automatically. Its other sections and English paragraphs stay in the design until you delete them, and many other infographic templates carry a PREMIUM label.

Changing the background colour (palette plus hex field) and the title font worked on Free; 'Create Brand Colors' and 'Upload Brand Font' asked for an upgrade. The app also sells one-off AI credit packs, from $20 for 2,000 credits to $200 for 25,000.
